decisions.question: How many tasks, and where to cut them (at most 4; every task but the last opens with a failing test)?

options.label: three tasks: values, then functions and renderers with the export list, then gate and doc
options.consequence: Task 1 lands graph.dart and findings.dart, everything the reject set (G1, G3) needs, so its replay moves from 11/3 to 13/1 with a checkable intermediate state; Task 2 lands the functions, the renderers and the 24-name export list and turns the replay to 14/14; Task 3 gates and writes the doc

options.label: two tasks: all declarations, then gate and doc
options.consequence: one reviewer gate for about 400 lines; no intermediate replay state; a rejected renderer choice would reject the findings too

options.label: four tasks: one per area (graph, analysis, json and render), then the doc
options.consequence: exceeds the 4-task cap with the doc task, or folds two areas anyway; the areas are 15 to 83 lines each, below a reviewer gate's worth

decisions.chosen: three tasks: values, then functions and renderers with the export list, then gate and doc
decisions.why: The cut follows what the fixtures check: the reject libraries need only the value types and their final fields, the surface library needs the functions and renderers too. A reviewer can reject the renderer or codec declarations while approving the values. The dry run shows each task's RED and GREEN exactly (T1.2, T1.4, T2.2, T2.4).
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md nidana.model.5 Size estimate (~8 files, <= 4 plan tasks)

decisions.question: Where does the GraphRenderer interface live, which D4 does not place (it names graph/ for ShellClaim and TopologyGraph, json/ for the codec and JsonRenderer, render/ for the Mermaid and Graphviz renderers)?

options.label: lib/src/graph/graph.dart beside TopologyGraph
options.consequence: TopologyGraph.render names it, so graph.dart is self-contained; render/, json/ and analysis/ import graph/ and the import graph is acyclic; render/ holds exactly what D4 names

options.label: lib/src/render/ with the Mermaid and Graphviz renderers
options.consequence: follows the contract's section split, but graph.dart and render/ import each other, and nidana.model.14, which fills render/, would share the file holding the interface json/ also implements

decisions.why: The interface and the graph name each other; keeping them in one library avoids an import cycle and leaves render/ to the two renderers D4 names. No guarantee depends on the file.

decisions.question: File names under the four areas D4 names.

options.label: graph/graph.dart, analysis/findings.dart, analysis/analyses.dart, json/codec.dart, render/renderers.dart
options.consequence: one library per area, two in analysis/ as D4 says (the findings and declarations in one, the analyses in another); eight files with the two tests, the estimate's count

options.label: one file per declaration family (claim.dart, topology_graph.dart, mermaid.dart, graphviz.dart and so on)
options.consequence: about twelve files for about 250 lines of declarations; more export directives

decisions.why: D4's wording names one library per area and two in analysis/; the names say what each holds. The later phases (nidana.model.10 to .14) fill exactly one area each, so parallel phases edit disjoint files as D4 intends.

decisions.question: The export list of topology_ir.dart and its form.

options.label: five export directives, one per src library, each with a show list, 24 names in ASCII order
options.consequence: matches the main library's and topology_plan.dart's form; exports_test.dart's reader handles show lists; the exact set is pinned in Task 2

options.label: export without show lists
options.consequence: any later helper in those libraries would leak; exports_test.dart's reader returns null for such a directive

decisions.chosen: five export directives, one per src library, each with a show list, 24 names in ASCII order
decisions.why: The precedent of the other two public libraries, and the step's requirement to pin the list by exact set. The 24 names are those of the four sections: Graphs 3, Renderers 4, The JSON form 4, Analyses 13.

decisions.question: How do ShellClaim and TopologyGraph get final fields when the Interface gives them only a factory, whose body computes and therefore throws this phase (D3)?

options.label: a private const generative constructor beside the throwing factory, under // ignore: unused_element with a one-line reason
options.consequence: the reject set's assignment_to_final holds (D2 shows a getter gives assignment_to_final_no_setter); two more suppressions until nidana.model.11 constructs through them; nidana.model.4's precedent for TransformEdge and TopologyDefinition

options.label: a factory that calls the private constructor without validation, copying or sorting
options.consequence: no suppression, but delivers partial semantics D3 leaves to nidana.model.11, and a test could come to rely on it

options.label: late final fields
options.consequence: a late final field without initializer has a setter, so assignment compiles and the reject set fails

decisions.chosen: a private const generative constructor beside the throwing factory, under // ignore: unused_element with a one-line reason
decisions.why: D3 and the confirmed reject codes require final fields and throwing computing bodies; the precedent is in the package already. The plan's Task 3 records the two suppressions as a dropped Learning.

decisions.question: What do the findings' and TopicNameCollision's generative constructors do this phase, given that G23's sorting is nidana.model.10's?

options.label: store their arguments as given
options.consequence: nidana.model.4's rule (generative constructors store their arguments); the tests build lists already in the Interface's orders, so they stay true after nidana.model.10 sorts

options.label: throw UnimplementedError
options.consequence: a generative constructor must initialize its final fields before a body can throw; the surface constructs findings at top level, which the replay does not run but consumers' tests would

decisions.why: Storing is not computing; the precedent is FunctionRef.named and MessageEnvelope. ScopeViolation and TopicDeclaration are const in the Interface, which only storing allows.

decisions.question: Which new classes carry @immutable, which the Interface's prose asks for every value type while its code blocks show none?

options.label: the value types: ShellClaim, TopologyGraph, the sealed TopologyFinding (for its four variants), TopicDeclaration, TopicNameCollision; not GraphRenderer or the renderers
options.consequence: follows the prose and nidana.model.4's EdgeInput precedent; applications implementing GraphRenderer are not forced to be immutable

options.label: every new class, the renderers included
options.consequence: annotates stateless behavior objects that G7 does not name as values; constrains application renderers

options.label: none, as the code blocks show
options.consequence: departs from the prose and from the IR declarations nidana.model.4 annotated

decisions.chosen: the value types: ShellClaim, TopologyGraph, the sealed TopologyFinding (for its four variants), TopicDeclaration, TopicNameCollision; not GraphRenderer or the renderers
decisions.why: The prose says value types; G7 lists which types have value equality, and renderers are not among them. No fixture depends on the annotation; the discrepancy is already routed to the end-of-nidana.model governance sweep (from S112).
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases (from S112)

decisions.question: The five trailing comments the formatter splits across two lines (TopologyGraph.topologies, .claims, .topics, WriterConflict.writers, TopicNameCollision.declarations): keep them trailing or move them?

options.label: on the line above the field
options.consequence: formatter-stable, readable, and nidana.model.4's precedent for TopologyDefinition.reads and .writes

options.label: trailing, as the formatter splits them
options.consequence: the type and the field name land on two lines (F), which reads worse

decisions.chosen: on the line above the field
decisions.why: The dry run's F step shows the formatter's split; the precedent moved the comment above.

decisions.question: The Interface writes the renderers as `{ const MermaidRenderer(); }` with no member; what does each declare?

options.label: the const constructor and an @override render(TopologyGraph) that throws
options.consequence: a non-abstract class implementing GraphRenderer must declare render; annotate_overrides requires the annotation

options.label: the constructor alone
options.consequence: does not compile (non_abstract_class_inherits_abstract_member)

decisions.chosen: the const constructor and an @override render(TopologyGraph) that throws
decisions.why: The only declaration that compiles; the Interface leaves the member implicit. Not a contract gap.
